title: JAS 39E / 39F Gripen

sources.title: Saab JAS 39 Gripen (Wikipedia), cockpit and avionics
Saab: Gripen E Wide Area Display
JoyPro cockpit catalog (panels, items and grip functions of the variant)

intro: The Gripen E (single seat) and F (two seats) are the newest Gripen, with a stronger engine (F414G), a new radar and a new cockpit: one wide touch screen replaces the three screens, under a small head-up display, and the pilot wears a helmet display. Buttons and knobs remain for the key functions. The grip functions are not public; they are taken here as those of the A/B, so the consoles and grips follow the A/B guide.

panels.name: Wide area display and HUD (E/F)
panels.text: The Gripen E/F replaces the three screens with one wide touch screen (Wide Area Display) under a smaller head-up display. A helmet display shows marks where the pilot looks.
panels.context: The pilot can split the big screen into pages as he likes and touch them; important functions can also be done with the stick and throttle buttons or with keys and knobs.

controls.name: Head-up display
controls.text: The glass screen in front of the pilot's eyes that shows flight numbers and aiming marks (head-up display). It shows speed, height, heading and the aiming marks, so the pilot can read them while looking outside.
controls.context: The pilot keeps his eyes on it during take-off, landing and every attack, instead of looking down at the instruments.

controls.name: Wide area display (WAD)
controls.text: One large touch screen across the whole front panel, about 19 by 8 inches. The pilot divides it into pages (formats) of his choice, such as the map, the sensors and the systems, and touches them to make choices.
controls.context: It shows the whole tactical picture in one place; Saab designed it so that the most important functions do not need touch.

controls.name: Display keys and knobs
controls.text: Real keys and knobs around the big screen. They do the key functions without touching the screen.
controls.context: Touching a screen is hard in a bumpy, high-G flight, so these give the pilot a sure way to work the important functions.

controls.name: Standby display
controls.text: Small backup instruments for attitude, speed and height. They keep working when the main screens or computers fail.
controls.context: The pilot uses them to fly safely home if the main displays are lost.

controls.name: Landing gear lever

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The wheels fold away into the aircraft.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The wheels come down and lock.

controls.text: This lever raises and lowers the landing gear, the wheels and their legs that fold away in flight.
controls.context: The pilot raises the gear right after take-off and lowers it before landing, then checks the gear lights.
